correctness.rationale: For two distinct positive queries x,y, common positive centers are q−2 points on their coordinate line when d_H(x,y)=1, exactly two switch-point centers when distance=2, or empty otherwise. Any third query splits the line into at most one versus the rest, hence the doubly positive candidate family has Ldim<=1; no complete adaptive depth-four tree exists. The packaged TREES.json depth-three witnesses for H(2,3), H(4,2) and depth-two H(3,2) are consistent with distance-one relations; independently computed exact finite Ldim via recursive candidate splitting, obtaining Ldim values 1,1,2,3,3,3,3 for (d,q)=(1,3),(2,2),(3,2),(2,3),(4,2),(3,3),(2,4). Product alphabet/dimension embeddings extend lower bounds, small neighborhood sizes give exceptional upper bounds. Read Adler–Benediktsson–Macpherson Theorem 4.7 in accepted full text: VC=3 exactly for d>=3,q>=3 or d>=2,q>=4 or d>=4,q>=2, and VC=2 at H(2,3). Thus unique strict Ldim>VC gap H(2,3). Infinite upper bound is structural, not inferred from finite enumeration.
